arxiv-1704-08670.title: The ZX calculus is a language for surface code lattice surgery
arxiv-1704-08670.creator: Niel de Beaudrap, Dominic Horsman
arxiv-1704-08670.description: Abstract A leading choice of error correction for scalable quantum computing is the surface code with lattice surgery. The basic lattice surgery operations, the merging and splitting of logical qubits, act non-unitarily on the logical states and are not easily captured by standard circuit notation.

arxiv-2104-06213.title: A zero forcing technique for bounding sums of eigenvalue multiplicities
arxiv-2104-06213.creator: Franklin H.J. Kenter, Jephian C.-H. Lin
arxiv-2104-06213.description: Abstract Given a graph G G , one may ask: “What sets of eigenvalues are possible over all weighted adjacency matrices of G G ?” (The weight of an edge is positive or negative, while the diagonal entries can be any real numbers.) This is known as the Inverse Eigenvalue Problem for graphs (IEP- G G ).

arxiv-2208-14082.title: Optimized Laser Models with Heisenberg-Limited Coherence and Sub-Poissonian Beam Photon Statistics
arxiv-2208-14082.creator: L. A. Ostrowski, T. J. Baker, S. N. Saadatmand, H. M. Wiseman
arxiv-2208-14082.description: Abstract Recently it has been shown that it is possible for a laser to produce a stationary beam with a coherence (quantified as the mean photon number at spectral peak) which scales as the fourth power of the mean number of excitations stored within the laser, this being quadratically larger than the standard or Schawlow-Townes limit HL .

arxiv-2309-06463.title: Neutrino mass models at μ \mu TRISTAN
arxiv-2309-06463.creator: P. S. Bhupal Dev, Julian Heeck, Anil Thapa
arxiv-2309-06463.description: Abstract We study the prospects of probing neutrino mass models at the newly proposed antimuon collider μ \mu TRISTAN, involving μ + ​ e − \mu^{+}e^{-} scattering at s = 346 ​ GeV \sqrt{s}=346\,\mathrm{GeV} and μ + ​ μ + \mu^{+}\mu^{+} scattering at s = 2 ​ TeV \sqrt{s}=2\,\mathrm{TeV} .

arxiv-2310-00391.title: On Yang–Mills fields from anti-de Sitter spaces
arxiv-2310-00391.creator: Kaushlendra Kumar
arxiv-2310-00391.description: Abstract Motivated by some recent progress involving a non-compact gauge group, we obtain classical gauge fields using non-compact foliations of anti-de Sitter space in 4 4 dimensions (required dimensionality for conformal invariance of Yang–Mills theory) and transfer these to Minkowski spacetime using a series of conformal maps.

arxiv-2410-22745.title: On minimal positive heights for blocks of almost quasi-simple groups Thanks: The first author gratefully acknowledges financial support by the DFG – Project-ID 286237555. The second author gratefully acknowledges support from the National Science Foundation, Award No. DMS-2100912, and her former ins
arxiv-2410-22745.creator: Gunter Malle, A. A. Schaeffer Fry
arxiv-2410-22745.description: Abstract . The Eaton–Moretó conjecture extends the recently-proven Brauer height zero conjecture to blocks with non-abelian defect group, positing equality between the minimal positive heights of a block of a finite group and its defect group. Here we provide further evidence for the inequality in this conjecture that is not implied by Dade’s conjecture.

arxiv-2511-19567.title: Pair density wave in the fractional quantum Hall effect at even denominator
arxiv-2511-19567.creator: M.V. Milovanović
arxiv-2511-19567.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by M.V. Milovanović. The fractional quantum Hall effect (FQHE) at filling 5/2, which is usually understood as a p p -wave paired state of underlying quasiparticles - composite fermions, transforms into a nematic phase under pressure csathy0 ; csathy . A pair density wave (PDW) may be a precursor, underlying state for this behaviour, and such state(s) were proposed that maintain the weak-pairing feature of the uniform paired state frad .

pmc-10562240.title: Risk of Revision After Vertebral Augmentation for Osteoporotic Vertebral Fracture: A Narrative Review
pmc-10562240.creator: Shinji Takahashi, Hiroyuki Inose, Koji Tamai, Masayoshi Iwamae, Hidetomi Terai, Hiroaki Nakamura
pmc-10562240.description: Osteoporotic vertebral fractures (OVFs) can hinder physical motor function, daily activities, and the quality of life in elderly patients when treated conservatively. Vertebral augmentation, which includes vertebroplasty and balloon kyphoplasty, is a commonly used procedure for OVFs. However, there have been reports of complications.

pmc-11328177.title: Fluorescent Nanocable as a Biomedical Tool: Intracellular Self-Assembly Formed by a Natural Product Interconnects and Synchronizes Mitochondria
pmc-11328177.creator: Xueqian Zhao, Fei Wang, Chuen Kam, Ming-Yu Wu, Jianyu Zhang, Changhuo Xu, Kai Bao, Qiyuan He, Ruquan Ye, Ben Zhong Tang, Sijie Chen
pmc-11328177.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Self-assembly processes commonly occur in various biological contexts to form functional biological structures. However, the self-assembly of nanofibers within cells by heterologous molecules showing a biological function is rare. In this work, we reported the intracellular formation of fluorescent nanofibers by a natural small molecule, lycobetaine (LBT), which facilitated the direct physical connection between mitochondria and synchronized their membrane potential oscillations.

pmc-13289388.title: Maternal BMI associations with cord blood DNA methylation and mid-childhood adiposity
pmc-13289388.creator: Grace Brolly, Miranda Gurra, Denise M. Scholtens, William L. Lowe, Marie-France Hivert, Jami L. Josefson
pmc-13289388.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundChildhood obesity is common and associated with adverse health outcomes. Fetal programming via epigenetics is a potential mechanism underlying its pathogenesis. We conducted an epigenome-wide association study (EWAS) on cord blood DNA to identify DNA methylation sites that may mediate the association of maternal body mass index (BMI) with offspring adiposity using data from the Hyperglycemia and Adverse Pregnancy Outcome (HAPO) Study and its follow-up study (HAPO FUS).

pmc-13297673.creator: Yasir Dilshad Siddiqui, Nusrat Sultana, Osama Khattak, Mohammed Zahedul Islam Nizami

pmc-13338479.title: Speed constant material perception via touch relies on natural material statistics
pmc-13338479.creator: Anna Metzger, Matteo Toscani
pmc-13338479.description: High-frequency vibrations from manual exploration of natural surfaces are crucial for differentiating materials. These signals depend not only on the spatial structure of materials’ surfaces but also on exploration speed. How we achieve speed constant material perception, even in passive perception in which the texture is moved across the finger, is an open question.

pmc-13368702.title: Association Between Participant Satisfaction and Self‐Reported Clinical Practice Behaviors in a Nationwide Guideline Education Program
pmc-13368702.creator: Kazuhiko Yamamuro, Kenta Ide, Yusuke Arai, Hiroyuki Muraoka, Toru Horinouchi, Yasushi Kawamata, Keisuke Mori, Shinichiro Ochi, Takashi Tsuboi, Hirotaka Yamagata, Hitoshi Iida, Yuka Yasuda, Junya Matsumoto, Naoki Hashimoto, Kazutaka Ohi, Toshiaki Onitsuka, Hisashi Yamada, Shusuke Numata, Hikaru Hori,
pmc-13368702.description: BackgroundEducational interventions are widely used to promote guideline‐concordant psychiatric practice. However, it remains unclear whether participants' subjective satisfaction translates into actual changes in clinical behavior (CB). This study examined the association between subjective assessment (SA) scores of the EGUIDE training programs for schizophrenia and major depressive disorder (MDD) and CB.

pmc-13619374.title: Intratumoral microbiota: implications for colorectal cancer pathogenesis and therapy
pmc-13619374.creator: Junhong Liu, Zhonghua Qi
pmc-13619374.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). CRC is the third most prevalent malignancy worldwide and the second leading cause of cancer-related mortality. According to GLOBOCAN 2022 estimates, approximately 1.93 million new CRC cases and 900,000 CRC-related deaths occur annually worldwide. Incidence rates continue to rise in developing countries, driven by the westernization of dietary patterns, sedentary lifestyles, and increasing obesity prevalence, with a notable trend toward younger-onset disease. In recent years, mounting evidence has implicated the microbiota as a critical contributor to CRC initiation and progression.

pmc-13621719.title: Does the biodiversity of urban green spaces impact on human health? A systematic review of literature
pmc-13621719.creator: Nicola Pelizzari, Carlotta Alias, Michela Tiboni, Anna Bertolazzi, Claudia Zani
pmc-13621719.description: Green spaces and their biodiversity seem to improve the urban life quality. However, a wide range of descriptors were associated with multiple health outcomes, which limits the comparability of existing evidence. The objective of this systematic review was to organise this knowledge, investigating the relationship between biodiversity in urban green spaces and health outcomes in adults.
